name: Five Finger Discount
description: Grab every cash bundle during the Prologue heist.
guide: The Prologue holds four cash bundles and two of them sit in rooms you pass through only once. Collect them before the alarm triggers, because the mission never lets you backtrack after the escape starts. Missing a single bundle means a fresh playthrough, since the Prologue has no mission replay.
why: The bundles are in one-time-only rooms, so one missed pickup locks the trophy out permanently.
steps: Search both offices before triggering the alarm.
Take the two bundles in the loading bay.
Start the escape only once the counter reads 4 of 4.

name: Quiet Professional
description: Complete an Ambrosia side job without raising an alarm.
guide: The pharmacy robbery is the cleanest job for this: wait until the clerk walks into the back room, then open the safe unseen. A single witness phone call voids the attempt even if you finish the job. The job is replayable from the activity menu, so practise the route instead of save-scumming.
why: It rewards a fully silent run rather than simple completion.
steps: Pick the pharmacy job from the activity menu.
Wait for the clerk to leave the counter before entering.
Leave without any witness calling the police.

name: Mail Run
description: Deliver twenty packages for the Ambrosia courier job.
guide: The courier job opens after the second Ambrosia story mission and pays poorly, but only on-time deliveries advance the counter. A motorbike through the alleys beats the main road every time. Twenty runs is roughly forty minutes, and the job stays open in free roam afterward.
why: It is a long, low-payout grind that most players skip entirely.
steps: Unlock the courier job after the second Ambrosia mission.
Finish twenty deliveries before each timer expires.
Check the job counter in the activity menu.

name: Gator Wrestler
guide: The race runs three laps through the mangroves and the AI cuts every corner tight, so hold the inside line at each marker. Boost on open water only, since the reeds stop the boat dead. It becomes replayable from the activity menu once the story hands you the airboat.
why: Winning means beating an aggressive field, not merely finishing the race.
steps: Unlock the airboat through the Grassrivers story.
Enter the airboat race from the activity menu.
Win all three laps without leaving the course.

name: Bog Hopper
description: Find all twelve swamp stashes in Grassrivers.
guide: Stashes hide under cypress roots and inside abandoned shacks, and the map only reveals them within a short radius. Sweep the region by airboat with the collectible filter switched on. Two stashes sit behind the story-gated hunting camp, so clear the Grassrivers missions first.
why: The set is region-locked and partly gated behind story progress.
steps: Finish the Grassrivers missions to open the hunting camp.
Sweep the wetlands by airboat with the collectible filter on.
Collect all twelve stashes.

name: Dock Worker
description: Complete twenty cargo jobs at Port Gellhorn.
guide: Cargo jobs are posted on the container yard notice board and each is a short forklift or truck run. Only undamaged deliveries advance the counter, so take the wet docks slowly. The board stays active in free roam, which makes this safe cleanup after the story.
why: The no-damage condition turns a routine delivery grind into a careful one.
steps: Take cargo jobs from the container yard board.
Finish twenty runs without damaging the cargo.
Confirm the count on the board.

name: Crane Operator
description: Crush a pursuing vehicle with a shipping container.
guide: The harbour cranes stay interactive outside missions, so lure a two-star pursuit onto the pier and drop a container as the car passes beneath the arm. The window is tight and each crane resets after one drop. Doing it during the Port Gellhorn mission that uses the crane is far easier.
why: It is an unmarked physics stunt that no objective ever points you toward.
steps: Get a two-star wanted level near the container yard.
Lure a police car under a crane arm.
Drop the container onto the car.

name: Reef Explorer
description: Discover every dive site in the Leonida Keys.
guide: Nine dive sites ring the islands and each needs a boat plus the rebreather the story supplies before the final Keys mission. A site only registers when you reach the wreck itself, not the surface buoy. Bring the treasure up on the same dive to skip a second trip.
why: It spans the whole island chain and requires underwater traversal at every stop.
steps: Unlock the rebreather through the Keys story.
Visit all nine wrecks by boat.
Surface at each site to register the discovery.

name: Island Hopper
description: Visit all nine Keys by boat without fast travelling.
guide: The counter tracks distinct islands reached by boat and silently resets if you take a taxi, plane or fast travel. Work from the northern tip south so the currents help instead of fight you. Stay docked at each island until the location name appears on screen.
why: It is an unlisted traversal challenge with a hidden reset condition.
steps: Rent or steal a boat in the Keys.
Dock at each of the nine islands in one trip.
Avoid all fast travel until the trophy pops.

name: Downtown Drifter
description: Win every Vice City street race.
guide: Eight street races run from the beach to Little Havana and each unlocks only after the previous win. Traffic is the real opponent, so race at night when the lanes are emptier. A fully upgraded sports car from the safehouse garage trivialises the later events.
why: Eight consecutive wins through live traffic is the city's biggest side-activity grind.
steps: Unlock street races through the Vice City story.
Win all eight races in order.
Check the race board for any remaining event.

name: Nightlife Legend
guide: Club jobs run on an in-game weekly timer, so they cannot be rushed in one sitting. Each week brings three tasks: restock, security and a VIP escort. Skipping a week stalls the chain but never fails it, so the trophy is slow rather than missable.
why: The weekly timer makes it a multi-session commitment instead of a single afternoon.
steps: Buy or inherit a club through the Vice City story.
Complete the restock, security and VIP tasks each week.
Finish the full management chain.

name: Paparazzi
description: Photograph ten celebrities around Vice City.
guide: Celebrity sightings are random events that surface as a camera icon once you are within two blocks. You need the phone camera raised and the subject framed, not simply standing nearby. Keep the camera equipped while cruising the beach strip to catch sightings without detours.
why: The encounters are random and never marked on the main map.
steps: Equip the phone camera.
Respond to ten celebrity sightings.
Frame and shoot each subject before they leave.

name: Rank and File
guide: Online ranks come from any activity, but races pay the most experience per minute. Join a public race playlist rather than free-roam jobs, since the playlist completion bonus stacks. The trophy pops mid-session the moment the rank bar fills, so let the session save before quitting.
why: It is the only long-form online progression trophy on the list.
steps: Join an online session from the pause menu.
Play race playlists until the rank bar reaches 25.
Finish the session so the rank saves.

name: Mountain Man
description: Survive three nights camping on Mount Kalaga.
guide: A night only counts if you sleep in the tent until dawn and wake without a wanted level. Cougars patrol the ridge after midnight, so keep a rifle loaded and the fire lit. The three nights do not need to be consecutive.
why: It forces exposed overnight survival in the game's most hostile region.
steps: Buy camping gear from the ranger station.
Sleep at a Kalaga campsite until dawn, three times.
Wake each morning with no wanted level.

name: Off-Road King
description: Win every Whetstone dirt track race.
guide: Five dirt events run the same circuit in different directions, and the loaner truck is deliberately underpowered. Bring your own tuned off-roader from the garage; the event allows it. Rain turns the track to mud, so check the forecast and race dry.
why: It is the region's full race series and demands a vehicle you supply yourself.
steps: Build or buy a tuned off-road vehicle.
Win all five dirt track events.
Race in dry weather to keep traction.

name: Big Game Hunter
description: Complete every hunting challenge in Whetstone.
guide: The ranger station posts six challenges, from tracking a boar to a clean one-shot on a buck. Clean means a single kill shot, so aim for the head or heart and never spray. The challenges unlock in order and each pays a small cash bonus.
why: The one-shot requirement punishes the spray-and-pray approach most players fall into.
steps: Take the challenge list from the Whetstone ranger station.
Complete all six in order.
Land a single kill shot on every animal.

name: Crew Cut
description: Finish the Heist with every crew member alive.
guide: Crew survival depends on the preparation missions you finished and the crew you hired, so complete every optional setup before the point of no return. Cheap hires die in the finale no matter how well you play. The outcome is decided before the heist starts, not during it.
why: Roster and setup choices lock at the point of no return, making it permanently missable.
steps: Complete every optional setup mission.
Hire the experienced crew members.
Finish the heist with all of them alive.

name: Clean Getaway
description: Escape the Heist with no wanted level.
guide: The storm drain route avoids every roadblock if you take the left fork at the tunnel. Do not fire a shot after leaving the vault; any kill restarts the pursuit timer. The trophy checks the wanted level at the instant you reach the safehouse.
why: It demands a silent escape from a mission built around loud action.
steps: Take the left fork into the storm drains.
Avoid firing on police during the escape.
Reach the safehouse with no wanted level.

name: Tourist Trap
description: Visit every region after the Epilogue.
guide: All ten regions must be visited in free roam after the credits, and the counter only ticks on arrival, so land or dock at each one instead of flying over. Mount Kalaga and the Keys are the two most players forget. The stats menu lists any regions still unchecked.
why: It is a post-story checklist that only becomes available in the Epilogue.
steps: Finish the story through the Epilogue.
Travel to all ten regions in free roam.
Check the stats menu for unchecked regions.
